intro.title: Explore Los Dos Templos
intro.description: Los Dos Templos is located in Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico. It is an important historical monument and landmark with rich historical and cultural value. The site is an important place to understand Mexican colonial history and architectural art, offering visitors a fascinating window into Mexican history and culture.

visitGuide.title: Visiting Tips
items: The site is open all day, daytime visits are recommended

alsoKnownAs.title: Highlights
items: Historical Monument: Important colonial historical landmark, symbol of Mexican architectural art.
Cultural Heritage: Located in Guadalajara, full of historical and cultural value.
Architectural Art: Experience Mexican colonial architectural styles and history.
Prime Location: Located in Guadalajara, Jalisco, easily accessible.

route.title: Tour Route
route.overview: Discover the ideal route to explore Los Dos Templos and experience the essence of Mexican history and culture.
steps: Arrive at the site in the morning to admire the surrounding historical buildings and ruins.
At noon, find a nearby restaurant to enjoy traditional Mexican cuisine.
Continue visiting in the afternoon to learn about colonial architectural styles and historical background.
After your visit, walk to Guadalajara historic center to see other attractions.
supplements: Please prepare some cash for buying souvenirs or snacks nearby.
The area around the site is open, please protect yourself from sun and stay hydrated.
If you are interested in history, you can prepare the historical background you want to learn about in advance.

sections.title: Historical Significance
sections.content: Los Dos Templos is an important historical and cultural site in Guadalajara. The site carries the historical memory of the colonial period and is an important place to understand Mexican history. The architectural style of the site reflects the artistic characteristics of the colonial period.

sections.title: Cultural Landscape
sections.content: The site is located in Guadalajara, surrounded by historically styled buildings. It's an excellent place to experience Mexican historical culture and architectural art, full of historical depth.

sections.title: Visiting Experience
sections.content: Visiting Los Dos Templos is an unforgettable historical and cultural experience. You can admire historical architecture, learn about Mexican colonial history, and feel the depth and charm of Mexican history.

historyTimeline.title: Historical Timeline

items.title: Colonial Period: Foundation
items.description: Los Dos Templos was built during the Mexican colonial period and is an important historical building site in Guadalajara. These two temple buildings reflect the unique architectural style and religious beliefs of that time.

items.title: 19th Century: Historical Changes
items.description: With historical changes, these two temples experienced multiple renovations and protections. They witnessed the development of Guadalajara and the evolution of history, becoming important cultural heritage.

items.title: 20th Century: Cultural Preservation
items.description: In the 20th century, with increased awareness of cultural heritage preservation, Los Dos Templos received better protection. The government and community worked together to ensure this historical site is properly maintained.

items.title: 21st Century: Tourism Development
items.description: Entering the 21st century, Los Dos Templos as an important cultural tourism attraction has attracted more and more visitors. It is not only a paradise for history enthusiasts, but also an important window to understand Mexican history and culture.

historyTimeline.guideContent: When visiting, start with the **site panoramic view** to feel the depth of history; then head to the **historical architecture** area to learn about colonial architectural styles; next, visit the **architectural details** to appreciate the traces of history; finally, understand the **cultural background** to deeply understand the important position of this site in Mexican history.
